title: Quentin and the Harvest
premise: Folklorist Vesper Oyelaran arrives in the dying village of Hollowmere to record harvest songs the locals refuse to sing twice, and when a church bell that was melted down in 1911 rings at midnight, she learns the village has quietly renewed an old bargain: something is invited in before every harvest moon, and it must be fed by dawn. Trapped in the churchyard with the village's last loyal son, Quentin, Vesper discovers her own recordings contain the true words of the original rite — proof of what was invited and who profited. As the thing wearing the bell's voice hunts them through the fields, she must choose between destroying the evidence (and her life's work) to break the bargain or keeping it and letting the village be taken. At sunrise she sings the songs back into the dark, unmaking the invitation, but the truth costs Quentin his life and leaves Vesper as Hollowmere's sole — and unwilling — keeper.
about_author: Ivo Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing parish records in rural coastal counties before turning to fiction. Their work blends documentary precision with folk horror, exploring what communities bury to survive.

chapters.title: The Songs They Won't Sing Twice
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She arrives in Hollowmere, tape recorder running, and coaxes fragments of harvest songs from elderly residents who go pale whenever she asks them to repeat a verse. The vicar warns her gently to leave before the moon fills. Emotional beat: scholarly fascination curdling into unease as she notices every song ends mid-line, cut off at the same word: 'come.'

chapters.title: A Bell with No Bell
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, closing on Quentin's. At midnight the melted-down church bell rings; the village doors lock from the inside, and Vesper is caught in the churchyard where the ground breathes. Quentin, the young warden sworn to the old rite, drags her into the vestry and confesses the bargain: something is invited in each harvest moon, and dawn is the only door out. Emotional beat: terror braided with the first spark of trust.

chapters.title: What Was Invited
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Vesper and Quentin. Playing back her field recordings, Vesper hears beneath the truncated songs the full original rite — and the name of the founding family who still profit from the feeding. The thing outside mimics voices, including Quentin's dead mother, testing their loyalty to each other against duty to the village. Emotional beat: love kindling under pressure as truth and loyalty begin to pull apart.

chapters.title: Until Sunrise
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. With minutes left, Vesper chooses to sing the complete rite backwards into the recorder and broadcast it through the broken bell tower, uninviting what was welcomed — knowing the evidence, and possibly herself, will burn with it. Quentin holds the door and does not survive the dawn. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into resolve as Vesper walks out alone, the village's secret now hers to keep or tell.
